item.title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen to have penalties
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc will both have 10-place grid penalties in Sao Paulo on Sunday [Getty Images] Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Verstappen will start from the back of the grid while Hamilton and Leclerc will both have 10-place penalties. They join Mercedes driver George Russell in having penalties for using too many engine parts. Russell's drop is only five places. Verstappen will have an an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc, Hamilton and Russell have all fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalties for the Ferrari drivers are bigger than Russell's because it is the first time they have exceeded the limit of four engines per season, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Rain is predicted overnight from Saturday into Sunday in the city this year, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." item.description: Former Real Madrid star opines on Vinicius’ situation: ‘They play better with Diomande’ Vinicius Jr.’s spot in Real Madrid’s starting XI is now under serious threat, or, for practical purposes, may well be gone. Some saw it as a much-needed reset for the Brazilian star, but as he prepared to return to league action after the international break, he will find Yan Diomande sitting comfortably ahead of him as Jose Mourinho’s preferred option on the left wing. Former player speaks on Vinicius Former Real Madrid and Spain striker Fernando Morientes spoke to the media earlier this week, where he opened up with his honest assessment of Vinicius Jr.’s situation and his competition with Yan Diomande. item.title: NBC solicits Brent Musburger, Bob Costas to narrate opening tease for Miami-Notre Dame
item.description: Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NBC Sports is giving Saturday’s Miami-Notre Dame matchup the big-game treatment with one of the network’s famous pregame teases. Before the Hurricanes and Fighting Irish kick off from South Bend at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, the network will give viewers a brief history of the recently renewed rivalry in the trademark style NBC Sports is known for. The opening tease begins with clips of Jimmy Johnson’s and Lou Holtz’s Miami and Notre Dame teams at the inception of what is now colloquially known as Catholics vs. Convicts before transitioning to the modern day, when a three-point Miami win in Week 1 of the 2025 season proved to be the difference between which team earned the final bid into the College Football Playoff just a year ago. And to add to the stakes, NBC has tapped two heavyweights to narrate the package. Brent Musburger, who called the original Catholics vs. Convicts game for CBS in 1988, narrates the tease alongside Bob Costas, who has lent his voice to many of NBC’s trademark opens throughout his time with the network. NBC has leaned into its history of producing narrative-setting opens for big games of late, particularly since the NBA returned to its airwaves last year. Many associate the style of these packages, and Costas’ voice, with Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls dynasty in the ’90s, and NBC Sports dutifully brought them back last NBA season to heaping praise. Now, the network will go back to the well for what is arguably the biggest college football game it will air all season. item.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc hit with Sao Paulo grid penalties in more Ferrari misery
item.description: Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix . The Ferrari duo have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA. The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday evening after Hamilton’s fury over his team-mate’s lap-one overtake on him in Mexico. Lewis Hamilton drives past a mural of Ayrton Senna in Sao Paulo (Bradley Collyer/PA) Hamilton questioned Leclerc’s mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks. Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend’s race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components. It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024. Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday’s race being affected. Formula One announced a five-year extension for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

item.title: Guernsey FC keep up winning run with 4-0 Lancing victory
item.description: Guernsey captain Ross Allen opened the scoring early on [BBC] Guernsey FC made it six successive wins in the Southern Combination Premier Division as they beat Lancing 4-0 at Victoria Park. Record goalscorer Ross Allen got the Green Lions off to a perfect start as he fired in from Dylan Graham's seventh-minute pass. Will Fazakerley crashed an effort off the crossbar four minutes later while Sam Murray headed against the frame of the goal form a corner moments later. Fazakerley found the net four minutes from half time when he turned in Dylan Graham's cross at the far post while the Green Lions went into the break 3-0 up after Murray finished after Archie Drillot's headed had come back off the bar. It took just two minutes of the second half for the hosts to further extend their lead - Graham was fouled in the penalty area and Allen converted from the spot. Corey Brouard shot wide with 15 minutes to go while Murray headed against the bar two minutes later. Related internet links Guernsey FC

item.title: Are the Badgers right to make a QB change to Ryan Hopkins?
item.description: MADISON, WI - SEPTEMBER 12: Wisconsin quarterback Ryan Hopkins (10) hands the ball off to Wisconsin running back Bryan Jackson II (21) during a college football game between the University of Wisconsin Badgers and the Western Illinois University Leathernecks on September 12, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Lawrence Iles/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are finally making a change at quarterback, as Ryan Hopkins will get his first career start against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, and looks to have the green light for Wisconsin’s final four games of the season. The Badgers, sitting at 5-3, have really struggled to throw the ball with starter Colton Joseph, who has completed under 56 percent of his passes this season, and has gone for fewer than 100 passing yards in three straight outings. The roughest one came last weekend against the Iowa Hawkeyes, as Joseph completed just 5 of 14 passes before being benched for Hopkins for the fourth quarter. Coming out of that game, Hopkins remains the starter, which a majority of fans looked for in our weekly Reacts poll. Wisconsin now faces Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue, and Minnesota in its final four games, so it should get an accurate look at Hopkins before making a key quarterback decision for the 2027 season. Was this the right time to make the quarterback change? Just a week ago, we saw reports that Wisconsin was negotiating with Colton Joseph for the 2027 season. But now, that feels unlikely, and it comes down to a rough transfer portal evaluation. Joseph just never improved the way the Badgers wanted him to, as accuracy and footwork issues were prevalent from the offseason and have carried throughout the year. He was a major work in progress coming into the season with his passing inconsistencies at Old Dominion, but his rushing ability was expected to provide a quality floor in the Big Ten. Still, Wisconsin’s offense has struggled a good amount, and moving to Hopkins feels like a much-needed move here at the end of the season. With jobs at stake, Wisconsin needs to see if Hopkins can be its guy next season or whether it’ll need to evaluate outside the program for its starter next year. At the very least, Hopkins looked confident as a passer last week, while dealing with some rookie mistakes. If he can build on that, Wisconsin has a chance to finish this season strong. It all starts on Saturday, when the Badgers take on Rutgers as 19.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel. But it’s another missed quarterback evaluation for the Badgers, and one that should create a lot of questions on process in the offseason.

item.title: Chris Bosh says change that has been made throughout the NBA was ‘definitely a mistake’
item.description: Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images Chris Bosh believes the lack of preseason games has been one of the reasons behind the rise of injuries in the NBA. The Hall of Famer played 70 or more games eight times in his career, which is a sensational achievement. In the current NBA, with injuries rising, not a lot of people are able to compete in a large number of games. Already, players like Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Anthony Edwards and Paolo Banchero are set to miss months due to injuries, which has led to an outcry among many to reduce the number of games per season. There has been no decision regarding the number of games being reduced, but the belief is that Adam Silver could be interested in trimming the game down to 40 minutes. No guarantee that playing fewer minutes will completely take away injuries, but Bosh knows what has led to the rise in injuries. Chris Bosh speaks on the importance of preseason The number of preseason games has reduced significantly in the past few years. CBA rules suggest that teams will not be allowed to play more than six preseason games. Despite this, very few teams use the full quota, and on average, franchises just give their players 3 to 5 games in the preseason. “I saw something really interesting over the weekend on RJ’s podcast, and he was speaking of how guys, especially the superstar guys, right? The guys who the team have paid them all their money to lead them, to score all the points, get all the rebounds, be the superstars that they are. And we expect these guys, going from a short training camp, only playing about one or two preseason games, to playing big minutes at a higher level, faster level, once the regular season starts. And that’s definitely a mistake,” said Bosh in a video that he uploaded online. “Before, we had eight preseason games. Maybe eight’s too much. I don’t know. But one thing that was for certain was that you were going to get in basketball shape, and even getting used to the movements, getting used to contact.” Richard Jefferson blasted the modern NBA players for not taking training seriously for the regular season and avoiding preseason. He used his own example to show how players today were not preparing well and jumping straight into the regular season, leading to a rise in injuries. “I do believe, watching Jalen Williams’ injury, it was really, really tough to watch. CBA rules suggest that teams will not be allowed to play more than six preseason games. Despite this, very few teams use the full quota, and on average, franchises just give their players 3 to 5 games in the preseason. “I saw something really interesting over the weekend on RJ’s podcast, and he was speaking of how guys, especially the superstar guys, right? The guys who the team have paid them all their money to lead them, to score all the points, get all the rebounds, be the superstars that they are. And we expect these guys, going from a short training camp, only playing about one or two preseason games, to playing big minutes at a higher level, faster level, once the regular season starts. And that’s definitely a mistake,” said Bosh in a video that he uploaded online. “Before, we had eight preseason games. Maybe eight’s too much. I don’t know. But one thing that was for certain was that you were going to get in basketball shape, and even getting used to the movements, getting used to contact.” Richard Jefferson blasted the modern NBA players for not taking training seriously for the regular season and avoiding preseason. He used his own example to show how players today were not preparing well and jumping straight into the regular season, leading to a rise in injuries. “I do believe, watching Jalen Williams’ injury, it was really, really tough to watch. I have to think if they had more practice time, if they had more preseason games, would his body have more balance, you know, and be able to take more contact in the air like that? And, you know, he still did land awkward, but I have to believe that playing more basketball gets you used to the basketball movements, used to taking contact, and it just gets you used to the overall pounding that your body has to take,” he added. “We felt that we had to get, you know, condition our bodies, get in shape first, get used to that contact, so then we could be able to go out and perform the games. We always said the games were the easy part because we pushed ourselves so hard in practice.” Injuries to star players is definitely not great for the league. They would want all players to stay fit, which is why they are looking into measures to reduce the risk of injuries. Whether the solution will be trimming games or minutes from games will be interesting to see, but even if that happens, Bosh’s point about practice and preseason taking precedence remains. He put up 30 points, 14 rebounds, and two blocks in only 26 minutes. It was another stellar performance that is only dimmed by that bright night against Dallas. MORE: Victor Wembanyama speaks on how the blood clot problem changed his outlook on life Wembanyama is playing with a chip on his shoulder after the disappointing end to the 2026 NBA Finals. "Of course, it’s always in the back of my mind, but it’s not my primary concern," Wembanyama said in French about his goals to win with the Spurs and win an MVP award . With the performances he is having for the Spurs, those two goals are feasible. It will be challenging, but it is possible because the Spurs' star player is ready to lead his team to victory by putting up gaudy numbers. The Cardinals made it clear to the Broncos that they have zero intention of trading the face of their franchise, and the Broncos have turned their attention elsewhere. Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Cardinals made it known they have no intention of trading away the face of their franchise. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they have zero intention of trading McBride, and Denver turned its attention elsewhere. This has been a move many Broncos fans have been wanting them to make, and despite being in the basement of the NFC West once again, the Cardinals do not seem keen on the idea of trading away their star tight end. Still, it appears the Broncos are big fish hunting ahead of the trade deadline and would like to add a playmaker to their offense prior to the deadline this coming Tuesday. As we know, they have been connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, but their level of interest seems to have lowered recently, with the New York Giants being the main interested team there. McBride would have been a huge and unexpected splash, so now we have to ask: what do GM George Paton and HC Sean Payton have cooking? It’s clear they want to add a weapon to their offense and are willing to make a big splash if they can. item.title: 😅 A mixed blessing?! Neuer's record match goes horribly wrong
item.description: 😅 A mixed blessing?! Neuer's record match goes horribly wrong By starting in Bayern's Bundesliga match against Mainz 05 today, Manuel Neuer overtook Bernd Dreher as FC Bayern's oldest-ever Bundesliga player. At 40 years and 225 days, he is now the oldest player to represent the record champions in the Bundesliga. And at first, everything went to plan. Kimmich put Bayern ahead in Mainz after 14 minutes, with Kane providing the assist. Then, in the 40th minute, things slowly but surely started going downhill, especially for record-breaker Manuel Neuer. Amiri swung a free kick into the box. Tah slightly deflected the delivery towards the far post, Neuer came flying out and missed it by a mile, and Jae-Sung Lee tapped in behind him for what appeared to be the equaliser. Immediately after his ill-fated and unsuccessful leap, Neuer signalled that something was wrong. After receiving treatment on his right foot, he had to come off, with Jonas Urbig replacing him. So Neuer is injured again, but there was still a silver lining. His mistake in misjudging the free kick went unpunished. Lee was narrowly offside when he scored, and after a VAR check, the goal was disallowed, leaving Bayern ahead at the break. What do you think of the incident? Let us know in the comments! item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. item.title: Wrexham owners' presence uplifting - Parkinson
item.description: Ryan Reynolds (left) and Rob Mac (right) took control of Wrexham in February 2021 [Getty Images] Phil Parkinson says the presence of co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac at Wrexham's draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers once again gave the club a significant lift. The Hollywood duo were in attendance as Lewis O'Brien's first goal of the campaign earned the Red Dragons a 1-1 draw following Adam Armstrong's opener at the Racecourse Ground. Following the draw, Parkinson stated everyone connected to the club is lifted when the duo attend a home fixture. "It's always very uplifting, I feel, for the people who work at the club, first of all, the players and the staff when Rob and Ryan come over," he said. "The crowd as well, they're uplifted by the owners being in town. "I communicate with them when they're back in the States, but equally it's good to have a chat with them when they're over." Wrexham claim point against in-form Wolves Wrexham chief executive Williamson leaves after two years The draw means Wrexham have claimed four points from their matches with promotion-hopefuls Middlesbrough and Wolves this week on the back of what was a disappointing 1-0 loss to Sheffield United last weekend. Following the defeat by the Blades, Parkinson raised concerns over the lack of a "Wrexham feel" to the display , something they rectified in fine fashion by beating Boro five days later. Having ensured they go into the final international window of 2026 in positive spirits, Parkinson stated the presence of Reynolds and Mac in north Wales has once again helped to highlight the importance of togetherness at the club. "Whatever division we've been in, when Rob and Ryan have been here, I think it's good for the players to see their connection with the club, how much they care and how much they're watching from afar," added the Wrexham manager. "Since day one we've been in it together. I always say that when we've done well and have got promoted, how everybody at this club has got this enormous togetherness and that starts from the very top." item.title: Packers Announce Unfortunate Micah Parsons Decision
item.description: The Green Bay Packers announced an unfortunate update on Micah Parsons on Friday. He is inching closer to returning to action but the team made a decision about his immediate future. The star pass rusher has yet to make his season debut after sustaining an ACL injury last December. He landed with the Packers in August 2025 via a trade from the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for defensive tackle Kenny Clark and two first-round draft picks. Parsons has established himself as one of the best players at his position and is a three-time first-team All-Pro and five-time Pro Bowler. He has recorded 297 combined tackles consisting of 106 assisted and 191 solo efforts in his career. Parsons also has 65.0 sacks, 75 tackles for loss and 11 forced fumbles under his name. Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Micah Parsons (1) during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field. Packers Reveal Micah Parsons’ Week 9 status Green Bay revealed that Parsons won’t be available to play on Sunday. The team has a Week 9 showdown with the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Zaire Franklin, Travis Glover, Sean Rhyan and Josh Whyle are also all listed as out . The Packers opened Parsons’ practice window on Wednesday. They have 21 days to activate him to their 53-man roster, proving that he is just a few more practices away from returning to the field. He is a game changer and will give the team a huge boost on defense. Green Bay is 5-3 this season and is coming off a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 8. The team has also won four of its last five assignments. However, the Packers remain at the bottom of the NFC North as all four teams have winning records. The good news is they have momentum on their side and will play their Week 10 game at Lambeau Field. Parsons and Co. will the have a bye week, making it likely that he sees action by Week 11 versus the Los Angeles Rams. item.title: Rory McIlroy rues double-bogey as Jon Rahm leads heading into final round in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Two-time major champion Jon Rahm shot a six-under-par 66 to give himself the outright lead heading into the final day of the Abu Dhabi Championship. After a slow start, the 31-year-old Spaniard turned up the heat on the back nine and went five-under thru nine holes, hitting an eagle between a pair of birdies on holes 10, 11 and 12 at Yas Links. He finished a shot in front of Englishman Tyrell Hatton and Italian Francesco Laporta, who are sitting on 17-under after rounds of 67 on day three. Jon Rahm holds the outright lead in Abu Dhabi heading into the final round (Getty) Rory McIlroy enjoyed a brilliant second day in Abu Dhabi and kept himself firmly in contention heading into the final day after going five-under for his third round – two shots behind leader Rahm. McIlroy hit eight birdies on day three but will be disappointed after a double-bogey on the 10th, which stopped him from finishing level with leader Rahm. The two-time Masters winner was pleased with the way he fought back, and said: “I played some really good golf out there but I’m also a little rueful. I felt like I had some really good momentum coming off the back of the front nine. “Just the bunker shot came out a lot faster than I anticipated, and then over the green and it was sort of dead from there. I followed another poor shot with another mistake at the third and ended up making a mess and made double. “But I fought back and made birdies on the next four holes. So it was a good bounce back. Overall, a good day. “If I can just limit the mistakes, there’s enough good golf. There’s enough birdies. There’s enough opportunities. I can play a clean round of golf tomorrow, I won’t be too far away.” Adam Scott sits on his own in fifth while David Puig and Englishman Matthew Jordan are a shot further back on 14-under.

item.title: Eagles QB Tanner McKee Responds to Benching News From Nick Sirianni
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles are going in another direction at quarterback — again. Tanner McKee was tapped to be the team’s starter under center after Jalen Hurts’ 2026 season was ended by blood clots found in his lung , but results have not been good for the Eagles, to say the least. McKee has now been benched by Philadelphia, as the team is going to hand the starting QB role to Joe Milton, who was signed by the Eagles off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad in October. Milton is expected to take snaps under center on Sunday, when Philly faces the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. Eagles’ McKee Sounds Off on His Benching After Three Starts Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles helmet rests on field against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Eagles went 0-3 with McKee as the starter, and that includes their 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 8 on the road. McKee, a former Stanford Cardinal quarterback, went 23/34 for 212 passing yards and zero touchdowns with an interception in that game. He also lost a fumble. “Obviously, as a competitor, would love to be out there as much as I can.” McKee said about getting benched, via EJ Smith of PHLY Sports . “I think when things happen that are unfortunate, you got to control what you can control, and you have to look inward, think of, you know, what can I do moving forward to better myself, better the team. And so that’s the approach that I’m going to have.” McKee also revealed how he learned from head coach Nick Sirianni that he’d be moving back to the bench. “Yeah, Nick called me. You know, it’s one thing I appreciate about, the 26-year-old McKee said. They’ve been very, you know, upfront about things. And, I know what he said in the media on Monday, the day before, but he said he wanted to communicate to the guys before, you know, he says anything to the media. He doesn’t want us finding out in the media, which I appreciate.” Tanner McKee said Nick Sirianni called him earlier this week to tell him he was getting benched. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/EtHctk8hil — EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) November 5, 2026 McKee was a sixth-round pick by Philadelphia in the 2023 NFL Draft. In three starts this season, he amassed 638 passing yards and two touchdowns against two interceptions on a 63.2 percent pass completion rate. The Eagles are heading to the New York game with a 2-6 record. item.title: Steelers’ Jaylen Warren Gets NFL MVP Endorsement From Ben Roethlisberger
item.description: Ben Roethlisberger seems to believe that people are sleeping on Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren , particularly in MVP conversations. Warren is having another solid season with Pittsburgh, and he is on pace to set a new career high in rushing yards. After his huge performance in the Steelers’ 27-6 demolition of the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh in Week 8, Warren got Big Ben feeling excited again over the running back’s prospect of winning MVP — or another major honor. “This guy needs to start to be talked about in some MVP stuff. Like league MVP or offensive MVP. His numbers and some of the stuff he’s doing is pretty impressive. His yards after contact have to be some of the highest in the league,” Roethlisberger said during a recent episode of his Footbahlin podcast (h/t Chris Ward of Steelers Now ). “There’s a lot of things that don’t look good and then all of a sudden it’s like, oh, he fell forward for three. Very rarely do you see him lose yards,” the Warren celebrated his 28th birthday in style on Sunday, as he lit up the Browns for 143 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. The Denver Broncos have explored the tight end market ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, including an inquiry about Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, as they seek more production from the position. Denver sits alone atop the AFC West at 6-2, but starting tight end Evan Engram has just 13 catches for 136 yards and one touchdown through eight games. He went without a reception on three targets in last week’s 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs. ESPN’s Adam Schefter detailed the Broncos’ interest Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, sharing an update from a trade-deadline report he co-wrote with Ian Rapoport. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Cardinals star Trey McBride , who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they… https://t.co/fz5M8XuzSF pic.twitter.com/7M5uZb4uKo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 7, 2026 McBride leads the NFL with 66 receptions on 86 targets this season after earning first-team All-Pro honors in 2025. That total includes 10 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos in Week 7, when Denver won 30-16 in Glendale. The star tight end’s Colorado roots add another layer to Denver’s interest. He grew up a Broncos fan in Fort Morgan and played at Colorado State, so a trade would bring him home to the team he supported as a child. Arizona’s stance on McBride comes despite its willingness to move other players. The Cardinals have already sent quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, showing that their deadline activity depends on the player involved. The full report indicates the Broncos turned their attention elsewhere after the Cardinals rejected the inquiry. It does not establish that the teams discussed compensation or that Denver submitted an offer for McBride. Engram’s contract expires after this season, adding a longer-term consideration at the position beyond Denver’s immediate needs. With Tuesday’s November 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, the Broncos continue searching for tight end help while the Cardinals remain unwilling to move McBride. item.description: (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Manuel Neuer continues to rewrite the record books, and this time, he has done it simply by stepping onto the pitch. The Bayern Munich captain has become the oldest player ever to appear for the club in a Bundesli ga match, achieving the milestone against Mainz. It is another remarkable achievement in a career that has already delivered just about every individual and collective hono r imaginabl e. Manuel Neuer becomes the oldest player to ever appear for FC Bayern in the Bundesliga ©️ pic.twitter.com/zI41sYxIaN — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 7, 2026 Neuer has been a fixture between the posts for Bayern Munich since arriving from Schalke in 2011, establishing himself as one of the greatest goalkeepers in football history. He has won multiple Bundesliga titles, Champions League trophies, and countless other hono rs while fundamentally changing expectations for the modern goalkeeper. Of course, Neuer has not exactly been taking the scenic route toward reti rement. Even as the years have added up, his ambition, competitive edge, and desire to remain Bayern Munich’s undisputed number one have remain ed evident. However, not even Neuer could escape the milestone without an issue. In the 40th minute, Nadiem Amiri’s free kick resulted in a bizarre sequence, which led to Mainz momentarily tying the match at 1-1. Amiri’s delivery glanced off the head of Tah, which led an airborne Neuer to not get a great touch on the ball. It deflected to Jae-sung Lee, whose header knotted the match at 1-1 — or at least that is what we thought. Neuer signaled for a sub and started to grab at his foot, which the Bayern Munich physios came out to look at. Ultimately, Neuer had to leave the match, but Lee’s goal was ruled offside by VAR in a very debatable call. Jonas Urbig replaced Neuer. Want to join in the game discussion? item.title: Browns’ Todd Monken Tells What he Truly Feels About Shedeur Sanders Ahead of QB’s Week 9 Start Against The Saints
item.description: There will be a different face handling the rock under center for the Cleveland Browns in their Week 9 game against the New Orleans Saints. With Deshaun Watson still on the concussion protocol , Cleveland will be going with second-year pro Shedeur Sanders as their starting quarterback for Sunday’s outing at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans. Cleveland head coach Todd Monken shares his thoughts on Sanders, as the QB gets ready for the Saints game. “He’s very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him,” Monken said, via Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN . “Just like any young player, they’ve got to play. … where he’s improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many things he needed to work on, and he’s done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position. And you can see that from the moment we got here and that’s why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent.” The Browns Hope Sander Delivers in His First Start in 2026 Campaign Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Watson started under center in Week 1 and had that job every week until getting placed on the concussion protocol following a Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. As Monken mentioned, this break for Sanders is an opportunity for the former Colorado Buffaloes star signal-caller to make a strong case for why he should be a QB1 for the team. Watson, a fifth-round selection by Cleveland in 2025, has played in only two games so far this season, both in relief. He’s gone 3/3 for two passing yards in those outings. During his rookie season, Sanders appeared in eight games with seven starts, passing for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns against 10 interceptions on a 56.6 percent completion rate. item.title: Formula One to race in São Paulo until 2035
item.description: Dutch Formula One driver Max Verstappen of team Oracle Red Bull Racing drives during free practice two at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Formula One to race in São Paulo until 2035») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Formula One will continue racing in São Paulo until at least 2035, having announced a five-year contract extension with the traditional host. The Autódromo José Carlos Pace in Interlagos first held F1 in 1973. On Sunday, the top racing series will take place for the 53rd time in Brazil, a country that has produced three world champions. "Brazil is an important part of Formula 1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in São Paulo until 2035," F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali said in a statement on Saturday. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of São Paulo." Brazil now boasts two regular drivers in Formula One - Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) and Rafael Camara (Haas). Austria and Miami have the longest contracts of all F1 venues, both running until 2041.

item.title: Ferrari duo to receive grid penalties in Brazil
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc pose for photos for the 2026 Formula One season. (is associated with: «Ferrari duo to receive grid penalties in Brazil») Ferrari/PA Media/dpa Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties in Brazil. The Ferrari drivers have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA. The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday after Hamilton’s fury over his team-mate’s lap-one overtake on him in Mexico. Hamilton questioned Leclerc’s mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks. Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend’s race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components. It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024. Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday’s race being affected. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli has already wrapped up the championship but Ferrari are still in the running for the constructors' championship, albeit trailing the Silver Arrows. Formula One announced a five-year extension for the grand prix in São Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

item.title: ‘A footballing alien’: Mamadou Sangaré soars to Premier League heights
item.description: Brentford’s Mali midfielder stood out when he was six and has shone in the Premier League since £39m transfer “When I first saw him, I thought to myself: ‘Who on earth is this player?’ laughs Youness Bengelloun as he remembers Mamadou Sangaré. With the transfer window in full swing in July 2025, the former Manchester City scout and agent was not expecting to come face to face with a “footballing alien”, but that proved the case during a visit to Rapid Vienna’s training ground. A few weeks later, Sangaré moved to Lens for around €5m. “He was impressive and what struck me was his technique and his work rate,” Bengelloun says. That’s more or less the impression Sangaré has made at every club he’s played for, including Brentford, for whom the Mali midfielder signed, from Lens, for a club-record £39m at the start of August. The 24-year-old excelled in his debut against Tottenham a few weeks later , dominating the centre of the pitch and providing the assist for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal, and has featured in every game this season, with Brighton up next. “I gave him his debut for Mali in September 2024, against Mozambique. He made an immediate impact,” says Sangaré’s former international manager Tom Saintfiet. “He’s every manager’s dream player.” Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
